# OSCAR

**Summary**: A framework that utilizes Accessibility Trees (A11y trees) generated by system APIs to represent GUI components for LLM agents, facilitating semantic grounding.
**Source Context**: Fundamentals of Building Autonomous LLM Agents.pdf

---

OSCAR is an example of a system employing [[concepts/structured-data-perception|structured data perception]]. It specifically uses the Accessibility Tree (A11y tree) provided by the Windows API (and potentially other platforms) as its primary environmental representation.

## How It Works
The A11y tree offers a hierarchical, structured representation of all GUI components (e.g., buttons, text fields, links), including their roles, states (like "unread"), and descriptive labels. OSCAR incorporates these labels to "facilitate semantic grounding," allowing an LLM agent to understand the purpose and function of each interface element programmatically [Source: Fundamentals of Building Autonomous LLM Agents.pdf].

This approach provides a precise, code-based understanding of an interface, which can be combined with [[concepts/multimodal-perception|visual perception]] methods for a more robust agent perception system.
